title: CMA CGM and DSV strengthen their partnership to accelerate low-carbon shipping through ACT+
summary: CMA CGM's ACT+ program, endorsed by DSV, targets a mere 12,000 tonnes of CO2 reduction over two years using second-generation UCOME-based biofuels. This "low-carbon" solution, touting an 83% CO2 cut compared to conventional HFO, likely operates on a book-and-claim system, offering little transparency on actual HFO displacement. Such tokenistic agreements do not address the urgent, fleet-wide decarbonization required to meet strict FuelEU Maritime targets and improve abysmal CII ratings across the broader fleet.
content:
CMA CGM and DSV have signed an agreement under which DSV will use CMA CGM’s ACT+ low-carbon shipping solution to support a targeted reduction of 12,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions over two years. These emissions reductions will be achieved through the use of low-carbon fuels, namely second-generation UCOME-based biofuels.

As part of its commitment to achieving Net Zero Carbon by 2050, CMA CGM has developed ACT+, its range of low-carbon transport solutions designed to help customers reduce their CO₂ emissions. Through this agreement, DSV will benefit from ACT +, which can help reduce CO₂ emissions by 83% compared to conventional shipping fuel, through the use of low-carbon fuels.

This partnership reinforces the long-standing relationship between CMA CGM and DSV and supports DSVs commitment to reaching net-zero emissions across its own operations and value chain by 2050. It also reflects a growing market trend, with DSV joining an increasing number of leading companies choosing or renewing their commitment to ACT+ as part of their decarbonization strategies.
